# Modified OpenHMD acquisition engine

Source: [Jan Schmidt's OpenHMD fork](https://github.com/thaytan/OpenHMD), branch `rift-kalman-filter`, commit [`a4ebf094e8be5c53c43c5f68d92e87afa5bdf0c8`](https://github.com/thaytan/OpenHMD/commit/a4ebf094e8be5c53c43c5f68d92e87afa5bdf0c8), dated 2026-07-29 ("rift: Backport pose metric tweaks from Monado"). Imported as source, without upstream history; this is a modified snapshot, not an unmodified upstream release.

Most source is under Boost Software License 1.0; dual-license files are used under their Boost option. `nxjson` retains MIT, and `miniz` retains Unlicense/public-domain terms. See the individual source headers, this directory's `LICENSE`, and the root `THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md`. The unused upstream GStreamer plugin and 3Glasses driver are omitted; other upstream hardware sources are retained but only the Rift driver is configured by cv1touch.

Local changes expose a bounded CV1 acquisition API, controller/radio decoding, factory geometry, timestamps, raw/labelled observations, optional PipeWire views, fixed calibrated camera poses, radio-only headset operation, and more resilient camera transfers. Tracking for cv1touch is performed in Rust. Native dependencies are resolved from the system; OpenCV 4 and 5 discovery is supported. The small nxjson UTF-8 encoder is replaced with an independently written Unicode-scalar encoder and boundary tests.

Compare this snapshot against the pinned upstream commit to inspect the complete modification set. Subsequent release changes are tracked in this repository. Preserve upstream notices when modifying or extracting code.

The UVC stream stop flag is atomic, and tracker teardown signals every stream before changing any USB alternate setting or waiting for transfers. Completion callbacks park failed submissions and return immediately; engine updates retry parked transfers at most once per 10 ms, including when no transfers remain in flight. This prevents a peer's retry loop from blocking shutdown or startup-failure cleanup while retaining recovery from transient submission errors. `test_uvc_shutdown` exercises peer shutdown, bounded retries, recovery, and frame lifetime without devices.

The CV1 extension exposes a controller's cached factory-calibration identity for binding optional user input calibration to that controller. The identity is copied when factory calibration completes; controller sample and shared-memory layouts are unchanged. Factory-normalized analog values remain unbounded at acquisition so the input-calibration guide can measure shifted endpoints; the Rust daemon applies user correction and bounds values before SteamVR publication.

Sensor discovery now owns a dynamically sized registry, and an additional configuration setter deep-copies complete ignore/pose lists without changing the existing scalar configuration ABI. Discovery rejects unusable/duplicate identities and cleans up failed starts. Constructors unwind partial allocations, and shutdown retains frame storage until analysis workers have joined. The unused fixed-size pose report array is replaced with a used-observation flag. Native tests cover discovery/configuration through 65 synthetic sensors, allocation failures, and outstanding-frame lifetime; practical USB/resource limits remain.

The engine's log goes to its C runtime's stdout. `ohmd_cv1touch_unbuffer_log` turns that stream's buffering off; on Windows the library carries its own C runtime, whose stdout is fully buffered when it is a pipe or a file, so the daemon calls it there.

`src/drv_oculus_rift/rift-sensor-blobwatch.c` uses an empty extent range on the first processed scanline without accessing a null previous line. The Linux native `blobwatch_ubsan` regression compiles blob extraction with UndefinedBehaviorSanitizer and recovery disabled; it covers dark and lit first scanlines, following extents, the last scanline, and repeated frames with both scalar and SIMD scanning.

UVC capture rejects incomplete raw images and damaged header/FID/PTS sequences before delivering a frame. Complete raw images are still delivered on the packet supplying their last byte, without waiting for EOF. After a delivered image, damage before the next boundary costs nothing, a new PTS starts the next image even if FID repeats, and only extra raw payload discards the following image. Before the first boundary after a stream starts, a header with a new presentation time also starts an image when the frame ID is unchanged, provided both headers carried a presentation time. The first packet after a stream opens is left over from an earlier stream: its timestamp predates this stream's clock. That clock restarts when the stream starts and runs at about 40 MHz. The first image arrives about 1 s later with frame ID 0 and a new timestamp. When the leftover also had frame ID 0, that image was rejected as out of sequence: on three five-sensor starts, four, four and two sensors, 145 to 157 packets each. An opening header without a presentation time does not start that image. A frame-ID change with the same presentation time remains a sequence error, including before that boundary. The opening packet's error flag is treated as before. JPEG images are delivered at a packet-ending outer EOI after SOS, or at EOF. Before SOS, the assembler skips marker payloads by their lengths so an APP thumbnail cannot end the main image. A structurally valid header establishes its frame boundary before its error flag is applied. Rejected candidates retain their assembler-owned buffer until reuse or teardown. Analysis also validates the exact packed GRAY8 layout. JPEG decoding rejects the libjpeg warnings that mean concealed damage (`JWRN_JPEG_EOF`, `JWRN_HIT_MARKER`, `JWRN_HUFF_BAD_CODE`, `JWRN_ARITH_BAD_CODE`, `JWRN_MUST_RESYNC`, `JWRN_BOGUS_PROGRESSION`, and `JWRN_EXTRANEOUS_DATA` before any marker but EOI) and keeps images with any other warning. The per-event UVC and JPEG messages are replaced by per-sensor summaries of discarded images by reason, at most one line every 10 s from the assembler and one from the decoder; malformed packets and repeated raw overruns continue to advance the reporting window without counting each packet as another image, and the buffer-starvation warning pair is unchanged. These checks remain partial: libjpeg-turbo can decode damaged entropy without a concealment warning, even through its slow Huffman path. Native fixtures exercise the real assembler, reused stale pixels through blob extraction, decoder recovery, the capture callback guard, log rate limits and frame ownership without opening devices.

A separate 56-byte sensor-video quality getter reports negotiated raw/JPEG input, accepted JPEG decodes and rejected image candidates, leaving the 40-byte acquisition record unchanged. Raw capture validates layout before advancing acquisition, still before any analysis lock. JPEG progress advances only after decoding and exact GRAY8 layout validation. Assembly and validation share a device-owned, relaxed-atomic rejected-candidate counter; malformed packets without an image, buffer starvation and intentional queue evictions are excluded. Neither counter reporting nor the getter waits for frame boundaries or changes exposure timing.
